goal: Make ANIMILL a dependable visual authoring application whose editor, viewer, timeline, saved project, standalone player, HyperFrames output, and Remotion output agree on the same composition.
definition_of_done: A creator can add, select, edit, time, layer, preview, save, reload, undo, and delete text and media without state drift or a dead control.
Paused, scrubbed, playing, standalone, HyperFrames, and Remotion views agree on visibility, timing, geometry, and base typography.
Legacy or incomplete project data is normalized atomically and invalid project data cannot corrupt the open project.
A representative multi-scene project completes both local MP4 render paths and is visually reviewed.
The primary workflow is understandable without knowing internal APIs or renderer terminology.
A creator can author, fit, zoom, scrub, save, and export a scene timeline up to one hour.
non_goals: Building the separate stickman flight-simulator project.
Adding more generation providers before the editor is stable.
Starting the audio-platform pivot before ANIMILL completion gates pass.
constraints: Preserve the existing ANIMILL workflow and user-created work.
Keep HyperFrames and Remotion explicit; never silently substitute one for the other.
Continue to support browser-local authoring and offline local rendering.
assumptions: The timeline is the source of truth for block visibility at the playhead.
Visual media belongs on the video track and text-native objects belong on text tracks.
The current single-page editor can be stabilized before a larger component refactor.
unknowns: Which advanced motion and effect families must have exact cross-renderer parity for the first stable release.
Which remaining controls are confusing in the user's normal screen size and project workflow.
Performance ceiling for long scenes with many blocks and simultaneous preview surfaces.

problem_formulations.question: What connected editing loop takes a user from adding an object to a trustworthy rendered result?
What must be true for the user to trust that exported video matches the viewer?
assumptions: visual parity is testable with representative frames

problem_formulations.question: What guarantees ANIMILL feels buggy even if renderer smoke tests pass?

decisive_evidence: Fresh browser interaction suite plus visual proof from both MP4 engines on the same representative project.
cost_risk: Exact parity for the full legacy effect catalog may require a shared effect specification rather than renderer-specific patches.

solution_equation: PERFECTED ANIMILL = canonical project state + reliable editor loop + timeline-true viewer + one-hour timeline authoring + shared interaction chrome + renderer parity + understandable workflow + representative end-to-end proof

modules.outcome: Old, generated, and current projects enter one safe canonical state.
interface_contract: Load is atomic; invalid input leaves the current project unchanged.
Blocks receive safe defaults and valid timing/track assignments.
acceptance: Fresh browser test loads a minimal legacy image block and rejects an empty project without state mutation.
fallback: Reject the project with a visible reason.
evidence: tests/ui-editor.test.mjs passes

modules.outcome: Text, geometry, timing, layer, opacity, selection, and undo controls mutate the intended object and refresh every consumer.
inputs: pointer, keyboard, inspector, command, and timeline actions
outputs: one updated canonical project and synchronized UI
interface_contract: Displayed controls are connected to model fields.
acceptance: Browser test proves live text edit and undo; manual audit confirms layer and opacity controls are connected.
fallback: Disable any control whose behavior cannot be made truthful.
evidence: tests/ui-editor.test.mjs passes
layer/opacity apply and command layer routing repaired

modules.outcome: The viewer always represents the current playhead and micro-effects cannot override object timing or transforms.
interface_contract: Before start and after end means invisible.
Motion transition and active duration are separate.
acceptance: Browser test proves an edit cannot reveal a future block; breath micro-effect cannot override hidden state.
fallback: Render without a micro-effect if it conflicts with the timeline transform.
evidence: tests/ui-editor.test.mjs passes

modules.outcome: Browser, standalone HTML, HyperFrames, and Remotion share timing, placement, and styling semantics.
interface_contract: Same base text alignment, padding, typography, geometry, and visibility.
acceptance: Both MP4 routes render fresh output; paired frames are visually compared; advanced effects receive a declared support result.
fallback: Mark an effect unsupported instead of silently changing its appearance.
evidence: Fresh HyperFrames and Remotion MP4 smoke renders complete
base typography and alignment parity repaired
Runtime capability report and server-enforced approval gate pass automated browser and unit tests
Exact rotate-in proof rendered successfully in both HyperFrames and Remotion

modules.outcome: A creator can discover the add-edit-time-preview-export path without prior ANIMILL knowledge.
outputs: visible tools, inspector, timeline, and plain-language guidance
interface_contract: Desktop advanced mode opens its essential panels.
Renderer additions appear at the export step rather than disrupting editing.
acceptance: User can complete a first edit and local export without command-line or API knowledge.
fallback: Provide a guided first-project mode while retaining advanced controls.
evidence: Desktop advanced mode preserves project aspect and opens tools/inspector
Five-step first-scene guide added
Real browser test completes edit, timeline, undo, and export-review interactions without console errors

modules.outcome: A creator can deliberately set and operate a scene timeline up to one hour.
inputs: active scene and requested duration from 1 to 3600000 milliseconds
outputs: bounded canonical scene duration and matching ruler, zoom, scrubber, playback, save, and export timing
interface_contract: One duration value drives every timeline consumer.
acceptance: Fresh browser test applies the visible one-hour preset and verifies the state, maximum, ruler, duration readout, and span readout.
fallback: Zoom into shorter windows while preserving the full canonical duration.
evidence: animill-studio/tests/ui-editor.test.mjs passes the one-hour authoring path
Visual review of the one-hour fitted timeline completed

modules.outcome: ANIMILL and connected authoring surfaces use one reticle light and hover language.
outputs: moving light, reticle state, hover feedback, and pointer information
interface_contract: Shared chrome cannot replace a stage block's motion transform.
Coarse pointers retain native cursor behavior.
acceptance: Fresh browser test proves ANIMILL and NANA share the pointer light and action-hover contract.
Pointer movement stays on a compositor transform layer above translucent authoring layers and hover feedback does not change control geometry.
fallback: Disable decorative light while retaining native pointer and focus-visible state.
evidence: animill-studio/tests/ui-editor.test.mjs shared chrome assertions pass
Regression proof covers 24rem light falloff, compositor transform movement, above-panel screen blending, fixed halo geometry, and zero-pixel hover layout shift
Fresh pointer sweep across Worlds reports no hover-related layout shifts

modules.outcome: A realistic multi-scene project proves the whole workflow under normal use and failure cases.
inputs: fresh multi-scene text, image, audio, and effect project
outputs: saved project, reopened project, standalone HTML, HyperFrames MP4, Remotion MP4, proof report
interface_contract: No stale outputs or mocked success.
acceptance: All artifacts created from the same fresh input and reviewed at several timestamps.
fallback: Narrow the stable release effect set and explicitly mark unsupported features.
evidence: artifacts/representative-proof contains one canonical three-scene project, standalone HTML, HyperFrames HTML, both fresh MP4s, six matched timestamp frames, contact sheet, and machine-readable proof report
Both render results are exact and complete
FFprobe confirms AAC audio in both MP4 outputs
Contact sheet visually reviewed across title, layered media, and finish scenes

integration_checks: Add text in the UI, change its content/timing/opacity, scrub before/during/after, undo, save, and reload.
Render the same representative project through standalone HTML, HyperFrames, and Remotion and compare frames at identical timestamps.
Attempt invalid and legacy loads and verify the open project remains usable.
Exercise narrow and desktop layouts with essential editing controls reachable.
Apply a one-hour scene length through the visible Scenes desk and verify every timeline readout uses it.
Compare shared reticle light and hover state in ANIMILL and NANA.
Sweep the pointer across empty space, controls, fields, clips, and stage blocks; confirm no layout jump and stable light tracking.
risks: The large inline editor script increases regression risk until stable boundaries are extracted.
Legacy CSS effects do not yet have complete equivalents in both production runtimes.
Browser object URLs remain session-only and cannot be consumed by server renderers.
Pointer feedback can regress into full-viewport repaint or layout translation if shared chrome adds animated background or transform rules.
One-hour authoring behavior is verified, but a full one-hour MP4 performance render is not yet benchmarked.
next_unlocked_capability: Continue the ANIMILL viewer, text, element-interface, and timeline fault sweep without adding unrelated features.
